packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

PACKET-07 - unverified image-only reading (working notes appended image by image; summary at end)

== image-001.jpg (reduced overview) ==
A long, narrow, wedge-shaped strip of paper or parchment on a black ground, laid horizontally; it tapers to a point at the left and is about 5 partial lines tall at the right end. Text runs left to right, parallel to the long edge. Brown ink, a cursive hand. No rubric, coloured initial, running title or column division visible. Only line 1 is nearly complete in height; lines 2-5 are cut diagonally by the lower tear, so each begins further right than the one above. Two small holes in the upper part. Too small to read; see tiles.

The upper edge is the diagonal tear, so the upper lines survive only at the right; the bottom line is the longest. No rubric, initial, running title or column division visible. One small hole near the lower edge.

== image-007.jpg (reduced overview, third face: an irregular upright fragment) ==
An irregular fragment, taller than wide, text upright, a single block about 22-24 short partial lines high. It appears to be two pieces: an upper piece with a straight left edge and a diagonal cut at top (lines of 2-4 words), and a wider lower piece with ragged edges; they meet at a tear with a blank-looking band between. All lines are cut at both ends, so no margin, column boundary, running title or rubric is certain. No coloured ink. Several lines are distinctly paler/blurred than their neighbours (possibly show-through or offset from the other side, or abraded ink - tentative). A darker stain near the centre of the lower piece.
Readable at overview scale only roughly; see tiles 008-010.

== image-010.jpg (reduced overview, fourth face: irregular upright fragment, apparently the other side of image-007's fragment, outline mirrored) ==
Irregular fragment, text upright, one block of about 24 short partial lines, slightly slanting upward to the right. Upper right: a paler patch (a different, overlying or exposed layer?) carrying about five short lines written at 90 degrees to the main text (reading bottom-to-top) - observation; whether this is a marginal note, a pasted-on scrap or an adhering piece of another leaf cannot be told from the image. A large letter resembling "P" stands in the middle of a line in the lower part, and a tall doubled vertical stroke (like "ff"/"ll" or a bracket) at the right edge lower down; no coloured ink. All lines cut at both ends.
Too small to read reliably; see tiles.

No rubric, coloured initial, running title, column gap or marginal gloss visible; a blank band along one edge at the narrow end (lower right as supplied = upper left when turned) may be margin - tentative.

PACKET-07 SUMMARY
================================================================
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author, or any earlier reading. I did not attempt to identify the text. The blue "K / UL" stamp on image-016/017 is a modern mark visible in the image itself; I record it only as an observation.
Beyond-the-rules disclosure: I made 180-degree rotated copies of image-014.jpg and image-015.jpg (written to a separate scratch directory) because that face was photographed upside down. I listed the two packet directories once at the start (file names only); I did not open packet.json. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

What the packet holds (six faces, apparently three fragments photographed on both sides - the pairing is inferred from mirrored outlines, tentative):
  A. image-001 (tiles 002-003) / image-004 (tiles 005-006): a narrow wedge-shaped strip, 4-5 partial lines per face, text parallel to the long edge.
  B. image-007 (tiles 008-009) / image-010 (tiles 011-012): an irregular upright fragment in two joined pieces, c. 22-24 short partial lines per face; one face carries a small patch with ~5 lines written sideways.
  C. image-013 (tiles 014-015, text inverted as supplied) / image-016 (= 017): a wide irregular fragment, c. 15-17 partial lines per face, with part of a left margin and (on 013/015) probably a top margin.
All are in brown ink in a small, rapid cursive book hand, heavily abbreviated Latin, single block of long lines as far as can be seen; no rubrication, coloured initials, running titles, ruling or systematic glossing are visible. Enlarged letters occur in the text line (a large "P" on image-011 L10; heavy "S"/"F"-like letters), and oblique strokes (virgules) and paraph-like signs punctuate. Whether any passage is lemma-plus-commentary cannot be decided from these scraps; the repeated formula on face 013-015 and the "de profundis clama.." repeated twice on image-005 L3 (and "clamor.."/"clamoris.. de profundo" in L4) look like a quoted phrase being expounded - tentative interpretation.

Spans chosen: I read every face, concentrating on (1) image-017 L5-L15 (best preserved; a connected passage on the seventh day / "septima die ... intelligitur" / "creationis et redemptionis" / "per sex dies"), (2) image-015 R1-R11 with image-014 R4-R14 (top of a written area; repeated "q.. [xps?] est ..." frame; "verbum ... assumendo"; "resurrectione.. / resurgendo"), (3) image-005 L3-L4 with image-006 ("de profundis clama.."), (4) image-009 L3-L11 ("... delicijs ... / sacra illa que prebentur ... / ... disputa.. In ... / potestatem ... accipimus / ... quicquid ... / ... quod sac.. / ..mentum / sacerdos"), (5) image-003 L1-L4.
Unread or essentially unread: the sideways lines in the patch on image-012; the pale/blurred lines on image-008 L14-15 and image-009 L1-2; the stained raised patch on image-014 R4-R5; smudged bands on image-015 R2-R3; most of the short left-strip line-stubs on image-012.

Limitations: every line on every face is cut at one or both ends, so no line is complete and joins between tiles are by overlap only. The hand is minim-heavy and strongly abbreviated; outside the handful of words flagged as secure, readings are letter-shape guesses with alternatives given after "/". Line counts on fragment B are approximate because of pale intervening lines that may be show-through. Column order / recto-verso order of the faces is unknown.
Suggested further views: a rotated (90 degrees) native crop of the sideways patch on image-012; rotated versions of image-013/014/015 as standard; raking-light or UV/IR images of the smudged bands on image-015 and the pale lines on image-008/009; a higher-magnification crop of image-003 line 1 and of the recurring "q + e.pt" group on image-014/015.
